function.name: read_alias
function.description: Read the current version at a visible workspace alias. Returns its exact reference and content. Does not adopt or hand off anything. Use read_version to choose an older exact version.

function.name: read_version
function.description: Read exactly the object_id/version_id you specify. Returns content and the same exact reference. No version is selected for you.

function.name: read_messages
function.description: Read actual messages addressed to this role, including requests and deliveries.

function.name: adopt
function.description: Bind an exact readable reference to a work input name. alias is the input name used later by sql_build, not an object ID. Reading and adopting are separate.

function.name: adopt_version
function.description: Explicitly move this existing non-fixed input adoption to a version you actually read. Supply the exact work_id, alias and version_id. This never edits the policy, builds a result or submits it. Fixed adoptions cannot advance.

function.name: write_object
function.description: Write a new version of the chosen local JSON alias. Explicit dependencies are exact source references; no source is selected or added automatically. A SQL project has models[{name,sql}], tests[{name,sql}], config{exports}.

function.name: sql_build
function.description: Execute the chosen SQL project using exact work adoptions named in input_aliases; write its real result/error to output_alias. SELECT/CTE only; no files/network/extensions. This is not a correctness judgment.

function.name: sql_query
function.description: Run one SELECT/CTE against tables in a local readable source or its exact work adoption. Save actual output/error to output_alias.

function.name: preflight_submission
function.description: Check public file, source, dependency and table structure only. Does not reveal correct business values, repair files or submit.

function.name: submit
function.description: Submit current versions of the chosen workspace aliases for the work. A submission alone is not approval or business correctness.

function.name: withdraw
function.description: Withdraw the specified pending submission before replacing it; prior files and reviews remain immutable.

function.name: inspect_submission
function.description: Inspect an exact real submission and its fixed artifact versions. Read the versions themselves before judging them.

function.name: raise_issue
function.description: Record a supported issue at an exact submitted object/version and nonempty locator path. Supply real evidence references and a specific description.

function.name: respond_issue
function.description: Respond to a real issue using the actual revised submission and exact evidence references.

function.name: decide_issue
function.description: Decide a real response after reviewing its actual revision and evidence.

function.name: approve
function.description: Approve this exact pending submission only after supported review. Does not supply evidence or make incorrect content correct.

function.name: wait
function.description: Advance world time by the declared ticks, allowing due transport events to run. Unlike staff_wait, this is a world action.

function.name: request_information
function.description: Ask a declared route provider for information for this work. Only a real provider decision can answer a manual route.

function.name: handoff_information
function.description: Choose evidence you actually read and send it through your manual route. Copy its exact reference. Omit request_id for proactive delivery, or provide the real request_id to reply. No adoption or approval is created. Your observation includes reply_options with exact scope fields for each pending addressed request. Copy the chosen request fields and supply evidence you chose; writing a body alone does not close a request.

mapper.scope: Carrier diagnosis only; no allocation method support inferred.

field_definitions.SourceRow: Original workbook row number including header offset.

data.scope: Only these complete selected invoices; no whole-customer-history inference.

source.attribution: Chen, D. (2015). Online Retail [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5BW33.

data.meaning: Apply the stated half-open source-local date interval. sales_only excludes InvoiceNo starting C/c and Quantity<=0; net_signed keeps signed quantities including cancellations. Both exclude missing CustomerID and UnitPrice<=0, retain source duplicate rows, and preserve all supplied customers with zeros. Final output uses integer GBP pence and counts distinct qualifying InvoiceNo.
data.origin: Simulated current client demand; not original retailer policy.

data.meaning: Raw UnitPrice is always GBP per unit. Select original rows using the exact client demand, sum Quantity*UnitPrice per CustomerID+InvoiceNo, and export amount in the declared unit. GBP means unchanged GBP; pence means GBP*100. Export exactly invoice_view(CustomerID,InvoiceNo,amount), customers(CustomerID), interface_meta(amount_unit). Export amount as DOUBLE so the existing managed SQL reader can load it; this finite slice has at most two decimal places, and the consumer rounds only final GBP pence. This unit is a simulated output-interface choice, not a change of original source meaning.
data.origin: Simulated source publication contract; no expected answer table.

models.name: invoice_view
models.sql: SELECT r.CustomerID,r.InvoiceNo,CAST(SUM(r.Quantity*r.UnitPrice)*(CASE WHEN s.amount_unit='pence' THEN 100 ELSE 1 END) AS DOUBLE) AS amount FROM retail r CROSS JOIN demand_meta d CROSS JOIN source_meta s WHERE r.InvoiceDate>=CAST(d.start_inclusive AS TIMESTAMP) AND r.InvoiceDate<CAST(d.end_exclusive AS TIMESTAMP) AND r.CustomerID IS NOT NULL AND r.UnitPrice>0 AND (d.invoice_mode='net_signed' OR (UPPER(SUBSTR(r.InvoiceNo,1,1))<>'C' AND r.Quantity>0)) GROUP BY r.CustomerID,r.InvoiceNo,s.amount_unit

models.name: customers
models.sql: SELECT CustomerID FROM raw_customers

models.name: interface_meta
models.sql: SELECT amount_unit FROM source_meta

models.name: metrics
models.sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT i.CustomerID,CAST(ROUND(SUM(i.amount)*(CASE WHEN m.amount_unit='GBP' THEN 100 ELSE 1 END)) AS BIGINT) AS revenue_pence,CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT i.InvoiceNo) AS BIGINT) AS invoice_count FROM invoice_view i CROSS JOIN interface_meta m CROSS JOIN demand_meta d WHERE d.invoice_mode IN ('sales_only','net_signed') GROUP BY i.CustomerID,m.amount_unit) SELECT c.CustomerID,COALESCE(t.revenue_pence,0)::BIGINT AS revenue_pence,COALESCE(t.invoice_count,0)::BIGINT AS invoice_count FROM customers c LEFT JOIN totals t ON c.CustomerID=t.CustomerID ORDER BY c.CustomerID

function.name: read_version

function.name: read_messages
function.description: Read actual messages addressed to this role, including requests and deliveries.

function.name: adopt
function.description: Bind an exact readable reference to a work input name. alias is the input name used later by sql_build, not an object ID. Reading and adopting are separate.

function.name: adopt_version
function.description: Explicitly move this existing non-fixed input adoption to a version you actually read. Supply the exact work_id, alias and version_id. This never edits the policy, builds a result or submits it. Fixed adoptions cannot advance.

function.name: write_object

function.description: Execute the chosen SQL project using exact work adoptions named in input_aliases; write its real result/error to output_alias. SELECT/CTE only; no files/network/extensions. This is not a correctness judgment.

function.name: sql_query
function.description: Run one SELECT/CTE against tables in a local readable source or its exact work adoption. Save actual output/error to output_alias.

function.name: withdraw
function.description: Withdraw the specified pending submission before replacing it; prior files and reviews remain immutable.

function.name: inspect_submission

function.name: raise_issue

function.name: respond_issue
function.description: Respond to a real issue using the actual revised submission and exact evidence references.

function.name: decide_issue
function.description: Decide a real response after reviewing its actual revision and evidence.

function.description: Approve this exact pending submission only after supported review. Does not supply evidence or make incorrect content correct.

source.attribution: Chen, D. (2015). Online Retail [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5BW33.

arguments.sql: SELECT InvoiceNo,CustomerID,Quantity,UnitPrice FROM retail ORDER BY SourceRow LIMIT 4

data.meaning: Raw UnitPrice is always GBP per unit. Select original rows using the exact client demand, sum Quantity*UnitPrice per CustomerID+InvoiceNo, and export amount in the declared unit. GBP means unchanged GBP; pence means GBP*100. Export exactly invoice_view(CustomerID,InvoiceNo,amount), customers(CustomerID), interface_meta(amount_unit). Export amount as DOUBLE so the existing managed SQL reader can load it; this finite slice has at most two decimal places, and the consumer rounds only final GBP pence. This unit is a simulated output-interface choice, not a change of original source meaning.
data.origin: Simulated source publication contract; no expected answer table.

data.meaning: Apply the stated half-open source-local date interval. sales_only excludes InvoiceNo starting C/c and Quantity<=0; net_signed keeps signed quantities including cancellations. Both exclude missing CustomerID and UnitPrice<=0, retain source duplicate rows, and preserve all supplied customers with zeros. Final output uses integer GBP pence and counts distinct qualifying InvoiceNo.

models.name: invoice_view
models.sql: SELECT r.CustomerID,r.InvoiceNo,CAST(SUM(r.Quantity*r.UnitPrice)*(CASE WHEN s.amount_unit='pence' THEN 100 ELSE 1 END) AS DOUBLE) AS amount FROM retail r CROSS JOIN demand_meta d CROSS JOIN source_meta s WHERE r.InvoiceDate>=CAST(d.start_inclusive AS TIMESTAMP) AND r.InvoiceDate<CAST(d.end_exclusive AS TIMESTAMP) AND r.CustomerID IS NOT NULL AND r.UnitPrice>0 AND (d.invoice_mode='net_signed' OR (UPPER(SUBSTR(r.InvoiceNo,1,1))<>'C' AND r.Quantity>0)) GROUP BY r.CustomerID,r.InvoiceNo,s.amount_unit

arguments.sql: SELECT InvoiceNo,CustomerID,Quantity,UnitPrice FROM retail ORDER BY SourceRow LIMIT 4

data.meaning: Raw UnitPrice is always GBP per unit. Select original rows using the exact client demand, sum Quantity*UnitPrice per CustomerID+InvoiceNo, and export amount in the declared unit. GBP means unchanged GBP; pence means GBP*100. Export exactly invoice_view(CustomerID,InvoiceNo,amount), customers(CustomerID), interface_meta(amount_unit). Export amount as DOUBLE so the existing managed SQL reader can load it; this finite slice has at most two decimal places, and the consumer rounds only final GBP pence. This unit is a simulated output-interface choice, not a change of original source meaning.

data.meaning: Apply the stated half-open source-local date interval. sales_only excludes InvoiceNo starting C/c and Quantity<=0; net_signed keeps signed quantities including cancellations. Both exclude missing CustomerID and UnitPrice<=0, retain source duplicate rows, and preserve all supplied customers with zeros. Final output uses integer GBP pence and counts distinct qualifying InvoiceNo.

function.description: Withdraw the specified pending submission before replacing it; prior files and reviews remain immutable.

function.name: inspect_submission
function.description: Inspect an exact real submission and its fixed artifact versions. Read the versions themselves before judging them.

function.name: raise_issue
function.description: Record a supported issue at an exact submitted object/version and nonempty locator path. Supply real evidence references and a specific description.

function.name: respond_issue
function.description: Respond to a real issue using the actual revised submission and exact evidence references.

function.name: decide_issue
function.description: Decide a real response after reviewing its actual revision and evidence.

function.name: approve
function.description: Approve this exact pending submission only after supported review. Does not supply evidence or make incorrect content correct.

function.name: wait
function.description: Advance world time by the declared ticks, allowing due transport events to run. Unlike staff_wait, this is a world action.

function.name: request_information
function.description: Ask a declared route provider for information for this work. Only a real provider decision can answer a manual route.

function.name: handoff_information
function.description: Choose evidence you actually read and send it through your manual route. Copy its exact reference. Omit request_id for proactive delivery, or provide the real request_id to reply. No adoption or approval is created. Your observation includes reply_options with exact scope fields for each pending addressed request. Copy the chosen request fields and supply evidence you chose; writing a body alone does not close a request.

function.name: staff_wait
function.description: Pause this worker without changing world time or business state. Use the actual world wait tool to advance world time.

function.name: staff_done
function.description: Declare this model worker stopped. This does not submit, approve or prove work correct.

data.meaning: Apply the stated half-open source-local date interval. sales_only excludes InvoiceNo starting C/c and Quantity<=0; net_signed keeps signed quantities including cancellations. Both exclude missing CustomerID and UnitPrice<=0, retain source duplicate rows, and preserve all supplied customers with zeros. data.meaning: Raw UnitPrice is always GBP per unit. Select original rows using the exact client demand, sum Quantity*UnitPrice per CustomerID+InvoiceNo, and export amount in the declared unit. GBP means unchanged GBP; pence means GBP*100. Export exactly invoice_view(CustomerID,InvoiceNo,amount), customers(CustomerID), interface_meta(amount_unit). Export amount as DOUBLE so the existing managed SQL reader can load it; this finite slice has at most two decimal places, and the consumer rounds only final GBP pence. This unit is a simulated output-interface choice, not a change of original source meaning.

function.name: read_alias
function.description: Read the current version at a visible workspace alias. Returns its exact reference and content. Does not adopt or hand off anything. Use read_version to choose an older exact version.

function.name: read_version
function.description: Read exactly the object_id/version_id you specify. Returns content and the same exact reference. No version is selected for you.

function.name: read_messages
function.description: Read actual messages addressed to this role, including requests and deliveries.

function.name: adopt
function.description: Bind an exact readable reference to a work input name. alias is the input name used later by sql_build, not an object ID. Reading and adopting are separate.

function.name: adopt_version
function.description: Explicitly move this existing non-fixed input adoption to a version you actually read. Supply the exact work_id, alias and version_id. This never edits the policy, builds a result or submits it. Fixed adoptions cannot advance.

function.name: write_object
function.description: Write a new version of the chosen local JSON alias. Explicit dependencies are exact source references; no source is selected or added automatically. A SQL project has models[{name,sql}], tests[{name,sql}], config{exports}.

function.name: sql_build
function.description: Execute the chosen SQL project using exact work adoptions named in input_aliases; write its real result/error to output_alias. SELECT/CTE only; no files/network/extensions. This is not a correctness judgment.

function.name: sql_query
function.description: Run one SELECT/CTE against tables in a local readable source or its exact work adoption. Save actual output/error to output_alias.

function.name: preflight_submission
function.description: Check public file, source, dependency and table structure only. Does not reveal correct business values, repair files or submit.

arguments.sql: SELECT InvoiceNo,CustomerID,Quantity,UnitPrice FROM retail ORDER BY SourceRow LIMIT 4

data.meaning: Raw UnitPrice is always GBP per unit. Select original rows using the exact client demand, sum Quantity*UnitPrice per CustomerID+InvoiceNo, and export amount in the declared unit. GBP means unchanged GBP; pence means GBP*100. Export exactly invoice_view(CustomerID,InvoiceNo,amount), customers(CustomerID), interface_meta(amount_unit). Export amount as DOUBLE so the existing managed SQL reader can load it; this finite slice has at most two decimal places, and the consumer rounds only final GBP pence. This unit is a simulated output-interface choice, not a change of original source meaning.
data.origin: Simulated source publication contract; no expected answer table.

data.meaning: Apply the stated half-open source-local date interval. sales_only excludes InvoiceNo starting C/c and Quantity<=0; net_signed keeps signed quantities including cancellations. Both exclude missing CustomerID and UnitPrice<=0, retain source duplicate rows, and preserve all supplied customers with zeros. Final output uses integer GBP pence and counts distinct qualifying InvoiceNo.

models.name: invoice_view
models.sql: SELECT r.CustomerID,r.InvoiceNo,CAST(SUM(r.Quantity*r.UnitPrice)*(CASE WHEN s.amount_unit='pence' THEN 100 ELSE 1 END) AS DOUBLE) AS amount FROM retail r CROSS JOIN demand_meta d CROSS JOIN source_meta s WHERE r.InvoiceDate>=CAST(d.start_inclusive AS TIMESTAMP) AND r.InvoiceDate<CAST(d.end_exclusive AS TIMESTAMP) AND r.CustomerID IS NOT NULL AND r.UnitPrice>0 AND (d.invoice_mode='net_signed' OR (UPPER(SUBSTR(r.InvoiceNo,1,1))<>'C' AND r.Quantity>0)) GROUP BY r.CustomerID,r.InvoiceNo,s.amount_unit

data.meaning: Apply the stated half-open source-local date interval. sales_only excludes InvoiceNo starting C/c and Quantity<=0; net_signed keeps signed quantities including cancellations. Both exclude missing CustomerID and UnitPrice<=0, retain source duplicate rows, and preserve all supplied customers with zeros. Final output uses integer GBP pence and counts distinct qualifying InvoiceNo.
data.origin: Simulated current client demand; not original retailer policy.

data.meaning: Raw UnitPrice is always GBP per unit. Select original rows using the exact client demand, sum Quantity*UnitPrice per CustomerID+InvoiceNo, and export amount in the declared unit. GBP means unchanged GBP; pence means GBP*100. Export exactly invoice_view(CustomerID,InvoiceNo,amount), customers(CustomerID), interface_meta(amount_unit). Export amount as DOUBLE so the existing managed SQL reader can load it; this finite slice has at most two decimal places, and the consumer rounds only final GBP pence. This unit is a simulated output-interface choice, not a change of original source meaning.

models.name: invoice_view
models.sql: SELECT r.CustomerID,r.InvoiceNo,CAST(SUM(r.Quantity*r.UnitPrice)*(CASE WHEN s.amount_unit='pence' THEN 100 ELSE 1 END) AS DOUBLE) AS amount FROM retail r CROSS JOIN demand_meta d CROSS JOIN source_meta s WHERE r.InvoiceDate>=CAST(d.start_inclusive AS TIMESTAMP) AND r.InvoiceDate<CAST(d.end_exclusive AS TIMESTAMP) AND r.CustomerID IS NOT NULL AND r.UnitPrice>0 AND (d.invoice_mode='net_signed' OR (UPPER(SUBSTR(r.InvoiceNo,1,1))<>'C' AND r.Quantity>0)) GROUP BY r.CustomerID,r.InvoiceNo,s.amount_unit

models.sql: SELECT amount_unit FROM source_meta

models.sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT i.CustomerID,CAST(ROUND(SUM(i.amount)*(CASE WHEN m.amount_unit='GBP' THEN 100 ELSE 1 END)) AS BIGINT) AS revenue_pence,CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT i.InvoiceNo) AS BIGINT) AS invoice_count FROM invoice_view i CROSS JOIN interface_meta m CROSS JOIN demand_meta d WHERE d.invoice_mode IN ('sales_only','net_signed') GROUP BY i.CustomerID,m.amount_unit) SELECT c.CustomerID,COALESCE(t.revenue_pence,0)::BIGINT AS revenue_pence,COALESCE(t.invoice_count,0)::BIGINT AS invoice_count FROM customers c LEFT JOIN totals t ON c.CustomerID=t.CustomerID ORDER BY c.CustomerID

function.name: read_alias
function.description: Read the current version at a visible workspace alias. Returns its exact reference and content. Does not adopt or hand off anything. Use read_version to choose an older exact version.

function.name: read_version
function.description: Read exactly the object_id/version_id you specify. Returns content and the same exact reference. No version is selected for you.

function.name: read_messages
function.description: Read actual messages addressed to this role, including requests and deliveries.

function.name: adopt
function.description: Bind an exact readable reference to a work input name. alias is the input name used later by sql_build, not an object ID. Reading and adopting are separate.

function.name: adopt_version
function.description: Explicitly move this existing non-fixed input adoption to a version you actually read. Supply the exact work_id, alias and version_id. This never edits the policy, builds a result or submits it. Fixed adoptions cannot advance.

function.name: write_object
function.description: Write a new version of the chosen local JSON alias. Explicit dependencies are exact source references; no source is selected or added automatically. A SQL project has models[{name,sql}], tests[{name,sql}], config{exports}.

function.name: sql_build
function.description: Execute the chosen SQL project using exact work adoptions named in input_aliases; write its real result/error to output_alias. SELECT/CTE only; no files/network/extensions. This is not a correctness judgment.

function.name: sql_query
function.description: Run one SELECT/CTE against tables in a local readable source or its exact work adoption. Save actual output/error to output_alias.

function.name: preflight_submission
function.description: Check public file, source, dependency and table structure only. Does not reveal correct business values, repair files or submit.

function.name: submit
function.description: Submit current versions of the chosen workspace aliases for the work. A submission alone is not approval or business correctness.

function.name: withdraw
function.description: Withdraw the specified pending submission before replacing it; prior files and reviews remain immutable.

function.name: inspect_submission
function.description: Inspect an exact real submission and its fixed artifact versions. Read the versions themselves before judging them.

function.name: raise_issue
function.description: Record a supported issue at an exact submitted object/version and nonempty locator path. Supply real evidence references and a specific description.

function.name: respond_issue
function.description: Respond to a real issue using the actual revised submission and exact evidence references.

function.name: decide_issue
function.description: Decide a real response after reviewing its actual revision and evidence.

function.name: approve
function.description: Approve this exact pending submission only after supported review. Does not supply evidence or make incorrect content correct.

function.name: wait
function.description: Advance world time by the declared ticks, allowing due transport events to run. Unlike staff_wait, this is a world action.

function.name: request_information
function.description: Ask a declared route provider for information for this work. Only a real provider decision can answer a manual route.

function.name: handoff_information

mapper.scope: Carrier diagnosis only; no allocation method support inferred.

field_definitions.SourceRow: Original workbook row number including header offset.

data.scope: Only these complete selected invoices; no whole-customer-history inference.

source.attribution: Chen, D. (2015). Online Retail [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5BW33.

data.meaning: Apply the stated half-open source-local date interval. sales_only excludes InvoiceNo starting C/c and Quantity<=0; net_signed keeps signed quantities including cancellations. Both exclude missing CustomerID and UnitPrice<=0, retain source duplicate rows, and preserve all supplied customers with zeros. Final output uses integer GBP pence and counts distinct qualifying InvoiceNo.
data.origin: Simulated current client demand; not original retailer policy.

data.meaning: Raw UnitPrice is always GBP per unit. Select original rows using the exact client demand, sum Quantity*UnitPrice per CustomerID+InvoiceNo, and export amount in the declared unit. GBP means unchanged GBP; pence means GBP*100. Export exactly invoice_view(CustomerID,InvoiceNo,amount), customers(CustomerID), interface_meta(amount_unit). Export amount as DOUBLE so the existing managed SQL reader can load it; this finite slice has at most two decimal places, and the consumer rounds only final GBP pence. This unit is a simulated output-interface choice, not a change of original source meaning.
data.origin: Simulated source publication contract; no expected answer table.

arguments.body: Use net_signed under this exact demand version.

data.meaning: Apply the stated half-open source-local date interval. sales_only excludes InvoiceNo starting C/c and Quantity<=0; net_signed keeps signed quantities including cancellations. Both exclude missing CustomerID and UnitPrice<=0, retain source duplicate rows, and preserve all supplied customers with zeros. Final output uses integer GBP pence and counts distinct qualifying InvoiceNo.

models.name: invoice_view
models.sql: SELECT r.CustomerID,r.InvoiceNo,CAST(SUM(r.Quantity*r.UnitPrice)*(CASE WHEN s.amount_unit='pence' THEN 100 ELSE 1 END) AS DOUBLE) AS amount FROM retail r CROSS JOIN demand_meta d CROSS JOIN source_meta s WHERE r.InvoiceDate>=CAST(d.start_inclusive AS TIMESTAMP) AND r.InvoiceDate<CAST(d.end_exclusive AS TIMESTAMP) AND r.CustomerID IS NOT NULL AND r.UnitPrice>0 AND (FALSE OR (UPPER(SUBSTR(r.InvoiceNo,1,1))<>'C' AND r.Quantity>0)) GROUP BY r.CustomerID,r.InvoiceNo,s.amount_unit

models.name: customers
models.sql: SELECT CustomerID FROM raw_customers

models.name: interface_meta
models.sql: SELECT amount_unit FROM source_meta

models.name: metrics
models.sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT i.CustomerID,CAST(ROUND(SUM(i.amount)*(CASE WHEN m.amount_unit='GBP' THEN 100 ELSE 1 END)) AS BIGINT) AS revenue_pence,CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT i.InvoiceNo) AS BIGINT) AS invoice_count FROM invoice_view i CROSS JOIN interface_meta m CROSS JOIN demand_meta d WHERE d.invoice_mode IN ('sales_only','net_signed') GROUP BY i.CustomerID,m.amount_unit) SELECT c.CustomerID,COALESCE(t.revenue_pence,0)::BIGINT AS revenue_pence,COALESCE(t.invoice_count,0)::BIGINT AS invoice_count FROM customers c LEFT JOIN totals t ON c.CustomerID=t.CustomerID ORDER BY c.CustomerID

data.meaning: Raw UnitPrice is always GBP per unit. Select original rows using the exact client demand, sum Quantity*UnitPrice per CustomerID+InvoiceNo, and export amount in the declared unit. GBP means unchanged GBP; pence means GBP*100. Export exactly invoice_view(CustomerID,InvoiceNo,amount), customers(CustomerID), interface_meta(amount_unit). Export amount as DOUBLE so the existing managed SQL reader can load it; this finite slice has at most two decimal places, and the consumer rounds only final GBP pence. This unit is a simulated output-interface choice, not a change of original source meaning.

models.name: invoice_view
models.sql: SELECT r.CustomerID,r.InvoiceNo,CAST(SUM(r.Quantity*r.UnitPrice)*(CASE WHEN s.amount_unit='pence' THEN 100 ELSE 1 END) AS DOUBLE) AS amount FROM retail r CROSS JOIN demand_meta d CROSS JOIN source_meta s WHERE r.InvoiceDate>=CAST(d.start_inclusive AS TIMESTAMP) AND r.InvoiceDate<CAST(d.end_exclusive AS TIMESTAMP) AND r.CustomerID IS NOT NULL AND r.UnitPrice>0 AND (d.invoice_mode='net_signed' OR (UPPER(SUBSTR(r.InvoiceNo,1,1))<>'C' AND r.Quantity>0)) GROUP BY r.CustomerID,r.InvoiceNo,s.amount_unit
